messages.author: a09dc4ba96c92dc8
messages.subject: Static Link to Shiny App
parts:
Hi,

I was wondering if anyone figured out, or if it's at all possible at the moment, to create something like a permalink to a particular input setting of a shiny app, similar to, say, how google maps lets you link to a particular location on the map by encoding the parameters in the html call. The application I have in mind is a dashboard with potentially many different outputs/plots, with the idea of pointing users to one of a few initial configurations that would be most common, rather than having the user tweak all the input controls every time they launch the app.


YT

messages.subject: Re: Static Link to Shiny App
parts:
Could you load() a .Rdata file with values for different inputs perhaps? You should be able to have an action button that load a specific .Rdata file and assigns the inputs to reactive values (don't think you can assign to input$...). If your functions use those reactive values ...

Maybe simpler ... load a series of values following a selection by the user and then use reactiveUI to set the default selections on various inputs dynamically.

messages.author: 80defc9c4046a73b
messages.subject: Re: Static Link to Shiny App
parts:
Looks like they have implemented this since the time of this post.

Have your server.R start like this...

shinyServer(function(input, output, clientData){
    query <- reactive(parseQueryString(clientData$url_search));
    ## other code where you reference the parameter named foo as query()$foo (within some sort of reactive expression)
})
